chunks: My father (may be pleased with himsaid: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Ali ibn Abdillah from Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad from Abi Hudhayfa from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) cursed those men who dress up as women and those women who dress up as men, and they are the effeminate men and those who marry each other. God destroyed the people of Lut only when the women performed the same acts as the men, and they saw each other.

key_terms.الْمُتَشَبِّهِینَ: Those who imitate or dress up like the opposite gender
key_terms.یَنْکِحُ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضاً: They marry each other (referring to homosexual unions)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the curse on the effeminate and those who emulate the opposite gender in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to highlight the specific curse upon the *Mukhannathun* (effeminate men) and women who emulate men, linking their sexual deviance to the unique destruction of the people of Lut. The text emphasizes that their downfall was precipitated when women began performing the acts of men, a detail that underscores the disruption of natural gender roles in Shia exegetical tradition. This hadith serves as a foundational proof for the prohibition of homosexual acts and the specific curse upon those who blur gender distinctions in conduct.
